Threadforge 1.0.25 is a maintenance release. Its dependencies have no known vulnerabilities, and the last traces of the Ultragravity name are gone.

- **No known vulnerabilities.** VulnWatch and npm audit report no findings for this release. Dependencies are updated within their ranges where possible; the build tools move to Vite 6 and Vitest 4, and the unused uuid and Tailwind CSS packages are removed. The interface itself does not change.
- **Mobile pairing certificate.** The certificate for phone pairing is now created with Node's built-in crypto instead of node-forge. It has the same contents. Already paired phones keep working with their saved certificate.
- **Threadforge name everywhere.** Remaining Ultragravity names in storage keys, events and styles are replaced. Saved settings move to the new keys once, automatically. The unused VS Code extension experiment and the old previous-product profile copy are removed.

Windows x64 NSIS installer with matching updater and checksum assets. Installed provider and UI acceptance follows the owner's manual testing.

The Toolbox ZIP contains the application payload from the original release above, without rebuilding or running it. Install it through Thread Toolbox; the original downloads are also retained.

A security maintenance release: two dependency updates for known advisories, with no changes to how Threadmap works.

## Install

Download **Threadmap-Setup-1.0.3.exe** below and run it. To update, install it over the earlier version into the same folder; your maps live in your repositories and are not touched.

The installer is not code-signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen warns the first time: click **More info → Run anyway**.

## What's new in 1.0.3

- The desktop app now ships **Electron 44.9.3** (was 44.4.3). This picks up the fix for [GHSA-x562-297c-g43g](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-x562-297c-g43g), where a pointer-lock permission request was attributed to the wrong frame (fixed upstream in Electron 44.5.0).
- The build tooling moved to **tsup 9**, which brings **esbuild 0.28.2** and the fix for [GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr), an esbuild dev-server file read on Windows. This affects the development build only; esbuild is not part of the installed app.

# ThreadNote 0.1.2

ThreadNote 0.1.2 is a security maintenance release. It moves Electron and
several dependencies to versions that fix published advisories. Application
code, data formats and settings are unchanged.

## Changes

- Updated Electron from 44.4.3 to 44.9.3. This fixes GHSA-x562-297c-g43g, where a
  pointer-lock permission was attributed to the wrong frame (moderate; fixed in
  Electron 44.5.0).
- Updated the MCP SDK (`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`) from 1.30.0 to 1.32.1, which
  fixes five advisories, including GHSA-46jr-4wx8-v453 and GHSA-6qxp-vccf-f47h.
- Updated `ip-address`, a transitive dependency of the MCP SDK, from 10.7.3 to
  10.7.4 (GHSA-rxp7-6hxx-x8q5).
- Updated `source-map-js` from 1.2.1 to 1.2.2 (GHSA-68fv-2mgg-jv7q). It is used
  by build tooling only.
- Updated Vite to 7.3.7 and Vitest to 5.0.5, with their lockfile dependencies.
  These are development tools and are not shipped in the packages.

## Downloads

- **Threadnote-0.1.2-setup.exe**: Windows x64 installer.
- **Threadnote-0.1.2-portable.exe**: standalone Windows x64 executable.
- **SHA256SUMS.txt**: SHA-256 checksums for the binaries and installer metadata.

Installed builds keep notes under `%APPDATA%/threadnote/` by default. Portable
builds use `ThreadnoteData` beside the executable. Settings → Data can select
another location. These builds use the project's existing unsigned configuration.

## Validation

- 528 tests passed across 58 test files; ESLint, TypeScript and production builds
  passed.
- The packaged version is 0.1.2 and the packaged runtime is Electron 44.9.3. The
  packages contain MCP SDK 1.32.1 and ip-address 10.7.4.
- All 19 production build/migration files and the runtime ICO match their
  sources; old smoke-test outputs are excluded.
- Application, installer and portable executable resources contain all seven TN
  icon frames and report product version 0.1.2.0.
- The installer and portable packages embed identical application files.
  Installer metadata size/SHA-512 and downloadable SHA-256 checksums are verified.

Native desktop UI checks are excluded by the browser-only verification policy.

Source commit: 58a8a54712735d05e9610c1dd032fe1a18075868.

# ThreadVoice v0.1.2

Windows x64 security maintenance release that updates Electron and the installer toolchain.

## Changes

- Updated Electron from 28.3.3 to **44.9.3** and electron-builder from 24.13.3 to **26.15.3**.
  This resolves the security advisories reported against the old Electron runtime and against the
  build toolchain (tar, app-builder-lib, builder-util-runtime and extract-zip).
- Moved clipboard paste and restore to the asynchronous clipboard API that Electron 44 requires.
  Dictated text is written, pasted and the previous clipboard contents are put back with awaited
  calls, and the clipboard snapshot now uses `clipboard.read()` / `ClipboardItem`.
- No other dependencies or features changed.

## Install or update

Download **ThreadVoice-Setup-0.1.2.exe** and run the installer. It installs for the current user and
creates desktop and Start menu shortcuts. Node.js is bundled. Installing over v0.1.1 preserves settings
and history. Configure your OpenAI API key in **Settings → Connection** if needed.

The installer is unsigned. Dictation and voice conversations require an internet connection and your
own paid OpenAI API access. Uninstalling preserves settings and history.

## Validation

- All 155 automated tests passed.
- TypeScript type checking and generated brand-resource checks passed.
- A fresh Windows x64 NSIS installer was built successfully with electron-builder 26.15.3; emitted and
  packaged brand-resource checks passed. The packaged app contains version 0.1.2, Electron 44.9.3,
  koffi 3.3.0 and the unpacked `uiohook-napi` 1.5.5 native module.
- Installer/app executable versions, update-metadata file size and SHA-512 checksum were verified.
  Release assets include the installer, blockmap, update metadata and `SHA256SUMS.txt`.

Verification was static only: the app and installer were not launched. In particular, the clipboard
restore after dictation was not exercised in the live app, and neither was the handling of files
copied in Explorer. No desktop UI was automated.

Threaduninstal v0.4.0 adds Windows Updates, a full update history and Office Click-to-Run rollback.

- **Windows Updates.** Lists the local Windows servicing packages, including older superseded updates Windows still records. Search by KB number or package name, filter installed/older updates and sort by date. One eligible update can be uninstalled through elevated DISM after confirmation, with an optional System Restore point and no automatic restart. Permanent and servicing stack packages are protected.
- **Update History.** Shows retained Windows Update attempts (Windows, drivers, Office and Store), Store/MSIX deployments and Office MSI patch events, with category/result filters, search and pagination. Collected records are archived locally, so rolling system logs do not erase history the app has already seen. A successful Windows record with one exact KB-to-package match can open the uninstall confirmation directly.
- **Driver and Office update removal** from History. Current OEM driver packages and registered Office MSI patches can be removed when they match exactly. Drivers use PnPUtil without force or automatic restart and list every affected device; critical and unknown device classes are blocked. Removing a driver can stop a device working and does not guarantee an older driver.
- **Office Click-to-Run rollback.** Choose an exact earlier Office build, check it on the active Microsoft channel, optionally create a restore point, then start Office's own signed updater with administrator approval. Automatic Office updates can be paused for 7 or 30 days; Windows Task Scheduler turns them back on afterwards, even with the app closed. Managed update sources, pending channel changes and open Office apps block the rollback.
- New headless reports: `--updates-report <json>` and `--update-history-report <json>`.
- Unchanged: application uninstalling, leftover scans, backups and restore work as in 0.3.0.

## Downloads

- **Threaduninstal-v0.4.0.zip**: portable app (`Threaduninstal.exe`, `assets/app.ico`, README, licences). This is the ThreadBox package.
- **Threaduninstal-v0.4.0.exe**: the same executable on its own.
- **SHA256SUMS.txt**: SHA-256 checksums of both.

Requires 64-bit Windows 10/11 with WebView2. Portable; no installer or account. Office rollback needs Internet access; everything else works offline. Close 0.3 before opening 0.4.

## Validation

69 Rust tests (update identity and eligibility, KB matching, history classification and archiving, driver and Office checks, Office pause scheduling, plus the existing uninstall, scan, backup and restore tests), TypeScript typecheck, and the release build. The packaged exe ran the read-only inventory and Windows Updates reports on a real machine. No real Windows update, driver or Office build was removed or rolled back; those paths were exercised with test fixtures and the browser preview.

Failing workflows across all your repositories, right on Home.

## Highlights

- **Failing workflows panel:** Home lists every workflow whose latest run on the default branch failed, across the repositories you own or collaborate on. Each row shows the failed jobs, the repository, the branch or tag, the run number and the commit. It also shows how many runs failed in a row, or that a newer run is already going.
- **Straight to the reason:** clicking a row opens that repository's Actions tab with the workflow selected and the failed run expanded, so the failure summary and annotations are visible right away.
- **Quick actions:** hover a row to re-run the failed jobs or open the run on GitHub.

## Notes

- The panel refreshes every 2 minutes while Home is open. It only checks repositories that have a `.github/workflows` folder, and uses about 90 GraphQL points per hour.
- Cancelled and skipped runs are ignored, and so are disabled workflows. A workflow counts as failing when its newest successful or failed run failed.
- Failures on pull request branches are not listed here; they show on the pull request rows as before.
- The installers are unsigned.

- `Threadboard_0.3.0_x64-setup.exe`: installer
- `Threadboard_0.3.0_x64_en-US.msi`: MSI installer

# VulnWatch 0.1.2

VulnWatch is a local vulnerability dashboard. It reads the lockfiles in your project folders (npm, Cargo, Go, Python venvs), matches the exact versions against OSV and GitHub advisories, rates them with CVSS, EPSS and CISA KEV, and opens Claude Code or Codex in the project to fix them.

## What's new in 0.1.2

**Accept for now.** Some vulnerabilities have no fix yet and never reach your apps. You can now set them aside with a note:

- Open a vulnerability and choose **Accept for now**. VulnWatch suggests a note from what it knows, for example "Build tools only; no fixed version yet."
- Accepted vulnerabilities leave Open, the project counts, the tray count and new-finding notices. They are listed with your note on the new **Accepted** page.
- An accepted vulnerability **comes back by itself** when a fixed version is released that wasn't there when you accepted it, when its severity changes, or when its priority rises (it starts shipping in an app, or CISA lists it as exploited). It shows a "Back" badge in Open, and VulnWatch sends a notification.
- From its panel you can accept it again or move it back to Open at any time.

Accepted vulnerabilities are stored in your VulnWatch settings, on this computer only.

## Windows downloads

- **VulnWatch-0.1.2-windows-x64-setup.exe**: Windows x64 installer.
- **VulnWatch-0.1.2-win32-x64.zip**: portable app (a single `vulnwatch.exe`). Install it through Thread Toolbox with `toolbox-manifest.json`, or extract and run it.
- **SHA256SUMS.txt**: checksums for the downloads.

Needs the Microsoft Edge WebView2 runtime (included in Windows 10 and 11).

## Validation

18 Rust unit tests passed, 3 of them new for the accept rule, and the TypeScript type check passed. The accept, restore and come-back flows were checked in the browser UI against a real scan of 41 projects. The installer was installed and started on Windows 11.

**ThreadBox:** the `win32-x64.zip` and `toolbox-manifest.json` provide a complete

The installer is unsigned. Windows x64 is the supported platform. The app is a
local workflow system and does not provide full n8n compatibility or its complete
